Renewed fighting between government forces and rebels has disrupted efforts to contain the disease. World Health Organization Ebola incident manager Dr Catherine Smallwood said fighting had prevented response teams from reaching some communities, disrupted contact tracing and reduced staffing at treatment centres. Health officials and WHO personnel have also been evacuated. The outbreak is caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain, for which no approved vaccine or treatment exists. items.excerpt: NEW YORK/LOS ANGELES, Nov 27 (Reuters) - Neither high fuel prices nor stubborn inflation are expected to stop US shoppers from spending robustly as their turkey hangovers wear off on Black Friday. But below healthy top-line forecasts lie signs of stress. Holiday spending — which unofficially begins on Black Friday — is seen topping last year’s strong figures by 4%-6%, several economic forecasts show. But most of the gains will be attributable to inflation which, at 3.8%, is about a percentage point higher than in each of the last two years. The National Retail Federation sees November-December holiday retail sales rising 4.2% year-over-year, to just above $1 trillion.

items.title: US economy roars ahead in third quarter, inflation remains high in October By Reuters
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Nov 25 (Reuters) - The US economy grew much faster than initially estimated in the third quarter, while inflation increased further in October, reinforcing expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next month and again in early 2027. The sharp upward revision to gross domestic product last quarter, reported by the Commerce Department on Wednesday, marked the quickest economic growth pace in three years. It reflected upgrades to consumer spending and business investment, mostly related to artificial intelligence. Robust domestic demand is fueling inflation, with a measure of underlying price pressures in October posting its biggest year-over-year increase since late 2023. The economy has powered ahead despite the ongoing US-Israeli war with Iran. "It is more urgent than ever that Fed officials step up the pace of interest rate hikes to cool off economic demand," said Christopher Rupkey, chief economist at FWDBONDS. "It was once thought that import tariffs and energy prices from the Mideast war were one-off factors behind the higher inflation numbers, but increasingly the inflation fires look to be stoked by old-fashioned economic demand pressures." GDP increased at a 4.3% annualized rate last quarter, the Commerce Department’s Bureau of Economic Analysis said in its second estimate of third-quarter GDP. It was the fastest pace since the third quarter of 2023. The economy was previously estimated to have grown at a 3.4% pace. Economists polled by Reuters had expected GDP growth to be revised up to a 3.5% pace. The economy grew at a 2.2% rate in the April-June quarter. Growth in consumer spending, which accounts for more than two-thirds of the economy, was revised up to a 4.2% rate. That was the strongest pace since the fourth quarter of 2024 and was an upgrade from the previously reported 3.8% pace. Spending is being driven mostly by higher-income households, whose wealth was boosted by the stock market before the ongoing AI-led selloff. Economists expect consumer spending to slow to a still-healthy pace in the fourth quarter, though declining gasoline prices should ease some of the financial pressure on middle- and lower-income households. ... The Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index increased 0.3% in October after gaining 0.5% in September, the BEA said. PCE inflation was lifted by higher prices for goods, including food and household furnishings, as well as services such as recreation, dining out and hotel stays. In the 12 months through October, PCE inflation increased 3.8% after advancing 3.6% in September. Excluding the volatile food and energy components, the PCE Price Index increased 0.3% for the third straight month. So-called core PCE inflation increased 3.3% on a year-over-year basis in October, the largest advance since November 2023, after climbing 3.1% in September. The Fed tracks the PCE price measures for its 2% inflation target. Financial markets have priced in a quarter-percentage-point rate hike at the US central bank’s December 8-9 meeting from the current 3.75%-4.00% range, and are expecting another increase in January, CME Group’s FedWatch tool showed.

items.excerpt: ## Democrat war over healthcare shows signs of an emerging truce ... House Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries endorsed a significant expansion of Medicare this month, including lowering the eligibility age, guaranteeing dental, vision and hearing benefits, and extending coverage to all children under 18. The top House Democrat’s backing could signal that the party’s progressive and centrist wings are ready to seek common ground on health care. The move drew praise from Sen. Bernie Sanders, author of the Medicare for All Act. Likewise, progressive Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed, a longtime advocate for universal health care, said he would accept a compromise that preserves private insurance. He compared such a system to public education, where “everybody is entitled to” attend public schools while parents remain free to pay for private education. That’s a major concession to moderates, who took issue with an existing Medicare for All bill that would end almost all private insurance. The post-election movement by both factions could reshape the debate inside the party and ease divisions on a contentious issue ahead of the 2028 presidential election.
